articles.title: Tyreek Hill’s divorce explodes as estranged wife demands answers on alleged bribery payoff
articles.standfirst: Court filings allege Hill hasn't fully answered questions involving former partner Crystal Espinal
articles.summary: Court filings allege Hill hasn't fully answered questions involving former partner Crystal Espinal
articles.body:
The legal fight between Tyreek Hill and estranged wife Keeta Hill is moving well beyond the end of their marriage, with the latest dispute centering on whether the former Miami Dolphins star improperly tried to influence a witness tied to his past.

According to court documents cited by TMZ, Keeta is asking the court to compel Hill to provide fuller answers about whether he offered, promised or paid “any consideration” to Crystal Espinal , his former partner and the mother of three of his children.

Keeta claims Hill hadn't spoken with Espinal in more than five years before one of his attorneys contacted her roughly a week before her scheduled deposition in the divorce case. The lawyer allegedly told Espinal there “needs to be trust” and that they “needed to bridge the gap.”

The filing further alleges that Hill then traveled to Arkansas to see Espinal and their children for the first time in two years.

Keeta wants answers over Hill’s contact with Espinal

The questions carry added weight because Espinal has previously made serious allegations against Hill , all of which require careful distinction from proven facts.

She accused Hill of physically abusing her while she was pregnant, allegations he denied.

The two were also involved in a 2019 child abuse investigation after concerns were raised about injuries to their son. A secretly recorded conversation that later became public included Espinal saying their son was “terrified” of Hill .

“You need to be terrified of me too, b*tch,” Hill replied in the recording.

The Kansas City Chiefs , his team at the time, barred him indefinitely from club activities during the controversy. The NFL later declined to suspend him after its investigation.

Keeta is now asking the court to make Hill clarify whether any payment, promise or benefit was offered to Espinal ahead of her testimony.

Filing raises allegations involving other women

The court battle doesn't stop with Espinal . Keeta also alleges that a woman named Sasha Iolani contacted her in April 2025 with a disturbing message.

“Despite everything you just went through with your altercation. I know how he gets. I was a victim of it for four years … stay resilient, you’re more powerful than you think,” the message allegedly said.

The filing also raises questions about another woman, Mila Kukarets , with Keeta alleging that Hill initially denied knowing her before changing his account after learning that messages existed.

The divorce itself was filed in 2025, one day after police responded to a domestic disturbance at the couple’s Sunny Isles Beach condominium.

Keeta ’s mother called police because she feared for her daughter’s safety. Keeta told authorities that Hill threw a laptop to the floor and took their daughter during an argument.

According to the police report, Hill said: “I have the same rights as a father as her as a mother, and I can take my baby whenever I want.”

The latest filing shows that Keeta wants far more disclosure about Hill’s contacts and conduct as the divorce fight continues to escalate.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill confirms one stunning truth hidden inside Daejon Love’s alleged fake NFL life
articles.standfirst: Love’s alleged NFL career was fake, but Hill revealed that one remarkable part of his story was apparently true
articles.summary: Love’s alleged NFL career was fake, but Hill revealed that one remarkable part of his story was apparently true
articles.body:
A lmost everything about Daejon Love’s alleged NFL life appeared to be invented. The San Francisco 49ers gear, the supposed contract, the claims that he had worked his way onto an NFL roster and the image of enormous wealth all formed part of a world that federal investigators say never truly existed. Then Tyreek Hill picked up his phone and complicated the entire story with a few simple words: “That’s my boy.”

Hill confirmed that he really knew Love and said the two used to train together . He even remembered Love running approximately a 4.2-second 40-yard dash, extraordinary speed even by professional football standards. “He really was nasty, though,” Hill said, using the football expression for someone with impressive ability.

Hill also suggested the now-viral clips of Love running routes on a beach were probably just him “trolling and having a good time.” For a man who had become an internet punchline for allegedly pretending to be an NFL receiver, it was an unexpected piece of validation.

The piece of truth that may have made everything else believable

According to investigators, Love did not immediately approach the women as strangers asking for money. He allegedly gained their trust through romantic relationships, spoke about building a future together and presented himself as a sophisticated investor with access to NFL money.

Chan allegedly joined video calls posing as his financial adviser and displayed fictitious investment gains. Once that trust had been established, the women were encouraged to transfer money or even obtain loans for opportunities that did not exist. Authorities say none of the identified victims received investment returns or repayments.

His supposed friendships with NFL stars were important pieces of that image. Love claimed Tyreek Hill, Antonio Brown and John Brown were close friends and training partners, using those connections to explain how NFL teams had supposedly become interested in him.

The claims looked like another part of the fantasy especially after John Brown publicly denied ever meeting him. Hill’s response, however, revealed that at least one of those relationships was real . Love had apparently trained beside one of the fastest and most recognizable players in football, and Hill believed he possessed genuine athletic talent.

Hill’s comments do not prove that Love played in the NFL, validate his alleged 49ers career or connect Hill in any way to the alleged fraud. There is no indication that Hill knew how Love may have been using their relationship. What his words do reveal is why the larger story may have sounded believable.

Love did not necessarily invent every person, workout or experience around him. He may have possessed enough real access to the football world to make the fictional parts of his life much more difficult to detect.

Love may never have been a San Francisco 49er, but he apparently stood close enough to real NFL talent to make that possibility feel real. That may be the most unsettling part of the entire story: the most convincing lies are often built around just enough truth.

The Department of Justice detailed the allegations against Love and Chan

That validation does not change the serious accusations surrounding Love. Federal prosecutors say the 35-year-old posed as a 49ers player or wealthy real estate investor while developing romantic relationships with women he met through dating apps.

Love and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, were arrested in Boise, Idaho, on August 24 and now face federal charges of conspiracy and wire fraud. Authorities allege they used false identities, fictitious investments and fabricated account balances to obtain approximately $1.3 million from at least 26 women across California, Oregon, Washington and Idaho.

Representatives for the NFL and the 49ers told investigators that Love had never been employed by either organization.

articles.title: OnlyFans model Celina Powell kicked out of Dolphins game and permanently banned from stadium
articles.standfirst: The influencer was removed during Miami’s preseason loss after alleged clash with security
articles.summary: The influencer was removed during Miami’s preseason loss after alleged clash with security
articles.body:
Celina Powell has made a habit of drawing attention at major sporting events, but her latest appearance in Miami ended with security escorting her out, and telling her not to come back.

The OnlyFans influencer has been permanently banned from Hard Rock Stadium after being removed during the Miami Dolphins ’ preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons , according to TMZ.

The incident reportedly began when stadium security asked Powell to move her feet from a wall in front of her seat. Witnesses told the outlet that she became confrontational and responded: “Shut the f*** up talking to me.”

Sheriff’s deputies were then called over to assist stadium staff, and Powell was escorted from the venue during Miami’s 17-12 loss. She later told TMZ that she had been informed the ban was permanent.

No plans to fight the decision

Powell said she was given the option of challenging the ban in court, but she does not intend to pursue an appeal.

That means one of Miami’s more recognizable celebrity spectators will no longer be permitted inside Hard Rock Stadium unless the decision is eventually reversed.

Powell has regularly appeared at sporting events around the city and has used those outings as part of her public persona.

She has previously spoken openly about sitting courtside at Miami Heat games and claimed she received contact information from several players after buying premium seats.

She has also made highly personal claims about past interactions with Heat guard Terry Rozier , remarks that generated significant attention online.

The Dolphins game, however, brought a very different kind of spotlight. Rather than leaving with new social-media content or another courtside story, Powell left with a permanent stadium ban.

Latest incident follows recent Miami arrest

The confrontation also comes shortly after Powell faced legal trouble elsewhere in the city. She was arrested in August for driving with a suspended license after allegedly accumulating 10 tickets for the same offense.

TMZ reported that authorities chose to take her into custody rather than issue another citation because of the repeated violations. Powell later said she planned to visit the DMV to resolve the issue.

She has also faced multiple Florida bench warrants connected to traffic violations after missing a December 2025 court date. Her attorney subsequently entered a not-guilty plea.

The Hard Rock Stadium incident now adds another chapter to a turbulent stretch. Miami has already completed its preseason and will open the regular season on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders on September 13.

The Dolphins will return to Hard Rock Stadium later in the month. Powell , however, won't be in the stands. At least not unless she changes course and decides to challenge the ban after all.

articles.title: De’Von Achane knee injury update: Dolphins RB says goodbye to the season in Week 3
articles.standfirst: The running back suffered the injury to his left knee during the 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The ACL tear leaves Miami without one of its main offensive pieces for the rest of 2026.
articles.summary: The running back suffered the injury to his left knee during the 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The ACL tear leaves Miami without one of its main offensive pieces for the rest of 2026.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins season suffered its hardest blow of the year so far after the worst medical fears were confirmed. Star running back De’Von Achane will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his left knee. The news was confirmed by the franchise’s medical team this Monday morning, after MRI studies revealed the severity of the damage he suffered during Sunday’s game.

Achane was injured during the Dolphins' first offensive series , on an 11-yard run. The running back planted his left leg to make a cut before falling to the turf and then being brought down. He was able to leave the field under his own power, but he went through the medical tent and was later taken to the locker room.

Miami loses one of its main offensive weapons

After the 24-10 loss to Kansas City , coach Jeff Hafley avoided offering an early diagnosis, although he acknowledged that the initial news was not encouraging. "To be completely honest, right now it doesn't sound very optimistic", he explained while the team awaited additional tests on the knee.

Achane finished the game with three carries for 17 yards and left the game with 10:42 remaining in the first quarter. Before facing the Chiefs, he had totaled 110 rushing yards on 31 attempts through the first two games of the season.

Achane's absence is an additional problem for a Miami offense that has struggled to produce in the first three weeks. The Dolphins are averaging 12 points per game and will lose one of their main weapons both in the running game and in the passing game.

Miami had included Achane in their long-term plans. General manager Jon-Eric Sullivan had described him as an important piece of the project and publicly ruled out the possibility of trading him. The running back agreed to a four-year extension during the spring.

The Dolphins will have to reorganize the backfield following Achane's injury. Jaylen Wright was unavailable against Kansas City due to foot issues and a stinger, so Ollie Gordon was the only running back available after Achane's exit.

The injury also comes at a difficult start for Miami. The Dolphins fell 24-10 to the Chiefs and dropped to 0-3. Their next game will be on the road against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4, now without Achane available for the rest of the season.

articles.title: The huge sum of money Tyreek Hill will have to pay Keeta Vaccaro after being found guilty of domestic violence
articles.standfirst: The former Miami Dolphins star has been ordered to pay his estranged wife $500,000 after a civil jury found him liable for two counts of battery, while rejecting several other claims
articles.summary: The former Miami Dolphins star has been ordered to pay his estranged wife $500,000 after a civil jury found him liable for two counts of battery, while rejecting several other claims
articles.body:
T yreek Hill has been ordered to pay $500,000 in compensatory damages to his estranged wife, Keeta Vaccaro , after a Miami jury found the former NFL wide receiver liable for two counts of battery in a civil case stemming from allegations of domestic abuse.

The verdict, delivered on Tuesday, October 13, marks a significant development in the legal dispute between the former couple.

However, the jury reached a mixed decision, finding Hill not liable for eight other claims brought by Vaccaro . She was also denied the punitive damages she had sought, according to multiple reports.

The case concerned alleged incidents during the couple's marriage, including confrontations in January 2024 and April 2025.

The jury found Hill liable for battery in both instances, with evidence relating to the April 2025 incident including footage captured by a nanny camera, according to reports from the trial.

The $500,000 award represents compensatory damages, intended to compensate Vaccaro for harm established in the civil proceedings. It is separate from punitive damages, which she also pursued but the jury did not grant.

It is important to distinguish the outcome from a criminal conviction: Hill was found liable in a civil lawsuit, not found guilty in a criminal domestic violence trial. The jury's decision applied to two specific battery claims, while Hill was cleared of the other eight claims considered by the jury.

Hill's attorney, Christi Bright , said her client was satisfied with the outcome despite the two findings against him.

“Mr. Hill was very pleased that he was able to get his story out and to be able to tell the world what he’s not been able to speak about,” Bright told reporters, according to ESPN. “He’s very grateful.”

What the jury heard during the civil trial

Vaccaro testified during the weeklong proceedings about what she described as a pattern of physical and verbal abuse. Among the allegations she raised was an incident in the summer of 2024, when she was pregnant with the couple's daughter, Capri.

“The first time he struck at my stomach and punched it and I saved myself,” Lakeeta said at the podium as she fought back tears. “He was like, ‘I don’t want the baby.’”

Hill denied that specific allegation, and the jury did not find him liable for that claim. Their daughter was born in November 2024.

The two battery findings related to separate incidents in January 2024 and April 2025. The latter involved nanny-camera footage that became a notable element of the trial.

Hill was allegedly heard calling Vaccaro a “broke bitch” during an argument, while the dispute also involved an alleged attempt to take their daughter from the home.

Hill denied physically harming Vaccaro in the incidents she described, although his testimony included an admission that he had made threatening remarks about getting other people to hurt her. He said he felt “deeply ashamed” about that statement.

The jury's decision did not resolve every allegation made during the case. Instead, it separated the claims on which Vaccaro established Hill's liability from those on which she did not prevail. The absence of punitive damages also means the final award was limited to the $500,000 in compensatory damages.

How the verdict could affect Hill's NFL future

The financial award arrives at a difficult time for Hill's football career. The five-time First-Team All-Pro receiver remains a free agent after the Miami Dolphins released him in February 2026. His departure followed a severe knee injury sustained during a game against the New York Jets in September 2025.

Hill spent the first six seasons of his NFL career with the Kansas City Chiefs , winning a Super Bowl with the franchise before being traded to Miami ahead of the 2022 season.

His explosive speed and production made him one of the league's most recognisable receivers, but his potential return to professional football now faces both physical and off-field uncertainty.

The Chiefs had reportedly contacted Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus , about a possible reunion as they considered options at wide receiver.

However, the team subsequently signed Justin Watson to its practice squad, and there has been no confirmation that Kansas City intends to bring Hill back.

The NFL is also conducting its own review under the league's personal conduct policy. Following the verdict, a spokesperson told Pro Football Talk: “We have been monitoring developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.”

The league's process is separate from the civil lawsuit, meaning Tuesday's decision does not automatically determine whether Hill will face disciplinary action or whether a team will sign him.

The NFL can assess the case under its own rules, while any interested franchise must weigh his football ability against the legal outcome and the broader circumstances.

For now, the clearest financial consequence is the $500,000 compensatory award to Vaccaro . The jury rejected several other claims and did not award punitive damages, but its findings on two counts of battery could have implications beyond the courtroom as Hill attempts to return to the NFL.

Whether he plays again remains uncertain. His potential comeback will depend not only on his recovery from injury but also on the league's ongoing review and the willingness of a team to offer him another opportunity.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill’s latest sprint raises concerns as NFL comeback talks heat up
articles.standfirst: The free-agent receiver is running again after a devastating knee injury, but his latest video appears to show that his stride is not fully back to normal
articles.summary: The free-agent receiver is running again after a devastating knee injury, but his latest video appears to show that his stride is not fully back to normal
articles.body:
Tyreek Hill is sprinting again, a meaningful sign of progress after the knee injury that ended his 2025 season. But in his latest training video, the eight-time Pro Bowl receiver appears to have a slight hitch in his stride. The clip shows him building speed, though his movement still looks uneven at moments, a detail likely to draw attention as NFL teams weigh a possible comeback.

Hill suffered a dislocated left knee and tore several ligaments, including his ACL, during a game against the New York Jets on Sept. 29, 2025. He underwent two surgeries, missed the rest of the season and was released by the Miami Dolphins in February. In a rehab video posted in July, Hill said he was still trying to regain power in his injured leg, even as he worked through running drills.

Tyreek Hill is running again, but his return remains uncertain

The latest sprint is encouraging because it shows Hill has progressed beyond basic rehabilitation and is testing himself at higher speeds . Still, a workout clip cannot show whether he has regained the acceleration, balance and change-of-direction ability required to play at the NFL level. Hill has not announced a return date, and the video alone does not establish that he is ready for game action.

His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Wednesday that Hill’s comeback discussions remain active, but that nothing is imminent. But there is no reported agreement, and any signing would depend on Hill’s medical evaluation and his ability to contribute.

On Wednesday, a Miami jury found him liable for two counts of battery in a civil case brought by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, and awarded her $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury found him not liable on eight other claims and rejected punitive damages. The verdict’s effect on his NFL prospects remains unclear, but it adds another factor teams and the league may consider.

For now, the video offers a hopeful but incomplete update: Hill is sprinting again and appears to be making progress, yet the hitch in his stride leaves a visible question about how close he is to full speed.

articles.title: Troy Aikman heading to ‘free agency’ as Dolphins role and ESPN future remain up in the air
articles.standfirst: Troy Aikman expects to become a free agent after the Super Bowl as uncertainty grows over his ESPN future and Dolphins advisory role
articles.summary: Troy Aikman expects to become a free agent after the Super Bowl as uncertainty grows over his ESPN future and Dolphins advisory role
articles.body:
Troy Aikman could enter the next NFL offseason facing uncertainty on two fronts, with his ESPN broadcasting contract approaching its end and his advisory connection to the Miami Dolphins lacking a formal long-term agreement.

The Hall of Fame quarterback reportedly earns $18 million annually from ESPN, but his deal expires after the season.

With no extension negotiations underway, Aikman has begun speaking openly about the possibility of becoming available to other employers once the Super Bowl is over.

Speaking to Dallas radio station 96.7 The Ticket, Aikman said he intends to complete the season before weighing his options.

“I think there’s probably a time and a place for all that to be discussed,” Aikman said.

“I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know that it’s hard to figure out kind of what’s happened. But I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens.

“But I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold and with the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be.”

He later told sports media reporter Jimmy Traina that the lack of contract discussions suggested ESPN could be preparing to move in another direction. The network hasn’t confirmed that conclusion, and reports have indicated discussions might still happen after the championship game.

Joe Buck’s extension adds to the uncertainty

Aikman’s situation has attracted additional attention because longtime broadcast partner Joe Buck recently signed a reported six-year extension worth approximately $108 million.

The pair have worked together for 25 years, first at Fox and later at ESPN, making them one of the longest-running NFL commentary duos.

Front Office Sports also reported that the broadcasters argued before a recent Monday Night Football game. Neither has publicly explained the reported disagreement in detail.

Aikman acknowledged there was a time and place to discuss what happened, while emphasizing that he remained focused on the season and looked forward to calling the Super Bowl, scheduled for February 14, 2027.

The uncertainty extends beyond television. Aikman advised Dolphins owner Stephen Ross during the organization's search for new leadership, which resulted in Jon-Erik Sullivan becoming general manager and Jeff Hafley being appointed head coach in January.

However, Front Office Sports reported that Aikman doesn't have a formal, ongoing consulting agreement with Miami. Whether he'll continue advising the franchise remains unclear.

A full-time front-office position could offer another path, either with the Dolphins or potentially the Dallas Cowboys, the team with which Aikman won three Super Bowls.

That kind of move would mean a significant career shift, and a football operations role might not provide the financial rewards available from another major broadcasting contract.

His Dolphins involvement also carries restrictions under NFL rules. Similar to Tom Brady , who holds an ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, Aikman can take part in virtual production meetings and conduct interviews away from team facilities, but he can't attend practices or appear inside the team's training facilities.

At this time Aikman hasn't announced his next move, and ESPN hasn't publicly confirmed that his tenure is ending. Whether the network returns to the negotiating table, a rival broadcaster makes an offer, or an NFL front-office opportunity emerges, the coming months will determine the next chapter of his career.
